label: copy-phase input token w
explanation: Fires when the token w is fed back as input during the copy phase (t > L), i.e. the model has just emitted w and is now outputting the original token that followed it. Never fires in the original phase or at <DEL>, even when w is input there (all activations are copy-phase; in_first=1 steps have zero activation). Covers ~99.6% of active steps and 99.9% of activation mass; residual ~0.1% mass is weak firing on copy-phase z. Magnitude grows with position in the copy: w fed back as the very first copied token (recall_idx 1) fires weakly or not at all (most false positives are there), while top activations are w at recall_idx 3-7 in long sequences. Adding recall_idx >= 2 raises precision to 0.87 but costs recall (F1 0.884 vs 0.880), so the simpler predicate is kept. Not sensitive to out_tok, prev_tok or digit content.

issues: The main claims hold. All activation is in the copy phase: 0 active steps in the original or delimiter phase on dev. in_tok w carries 99.9% of activation mass and z about 0.1%. correct==0 has essentially no firing, and out_tok, prev_tok and digit content show flat lift.

The false positives follow a pattern, and the explanation describes it wrongly. Whether copy-phase w fires depends mainly on absolute step t, i.e. on sequence length, not on recall_idx alone. Dev precision of the predicate within each t bucket: t<=6 0.31, t=7 0.52, t=8 0.69, t=9 0.76, t=10 0.85, t>=11 0.94. By L: L<=4 0.36, L=5 0.63, L>=6 0.86. At the same recall_idx, length still matters: recall_idx 1 gives 0.42 overall but 0.66 when L>=8. recall_idx>=3 still drops to 0.42 when L<=4. So 'weak or absent at recall_idx 1' is a side effect of an early-t / short-sequence effect.

The explanation's chosen refinement was recall_idx>=2, which barely helps (dev F1 0.884). Filtering on absolute step does better: (phase==2)&(in_tok==w)&(t>=7) scores test P 0.841 / R 0.960 / F1 0.896 / mass recall 0.983, against 0.791 / 0.996 / 0.882 / 0.999 for the original predicate.

The test-split false positives are inactive w inputs early in the copy, often in short sequences, e.g. 'v d w 0 <DEL> v d *w*' and 'q w 1 j <DEL> q *w* 1'. This is the same structured class, not scattered noise.
